In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
6-OH DA, a chemical sympathectomy agent, prevents salt-induced hypertension in Dahl S rats by lowering sympathetic tone in the hindquarters.

chemical sympatectomy" with the neurotoxin 6-hydrodopamine (100 mg/kg, ip) prevents the development of salt induced hypertension, salt induced increased in hindquarters resistance, and salt induced increased in neurogenic vasoconstictor tone in Dahl salt sensitive rats.

chemical sympatectomy" with the neurotoxin 6-OH-DA prevents salt-induced hypertension in Dahl S rats, suggesting that the sympathetic nervous system contributes to the salt-induced hypertension in this model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the salt-induced hypertension in Dahl S rats is mediated by both humoral and neurogenic mechanisms.
the sympathetic nervous system plays a major role in salt-induced hypertension in Dahl salt-sensitive rats.
neurogenic mechanisms are important in salt-sensitive hypertension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the development of salt-sensitive hypertension is due to the sympathetic nervous system and not to humoral mechanisms, such as angiotensin II.

salt-induced hypertension is a complex phenomenon that involves a variety of factors and that the sympathetic nervous system is one of the factors involved in the genesis of salt-induced hypertension.

the sympathetic nervous system is a key player in the development of hypertension in Dahl S rats and that the sympathetic system may be a good target for the treatment and prevention of salt-induced hypertension.
